_: v0.29.9 D5/D7 — `related` evaluated over the shipped artifact, pinned as shared vectors.
Two implementations evaluate one artifact on opposite ends of the sync wire: the api's lexical
arm (cosine over the per-note vectors, then core's `fuse`) and the CLI's `docli related`
(the same cosine from docli-rules, its own fifteen-line RRF). They ship on different release
trains, so this file is the contract.
SEQUENCE is pinned here, unlike graph.json: `related` is a ranked list and its parity claim is
rank order. Fusion breaks score ties by PATH under Rust `String::cmp` on both sides — byte
order, no collation anywhere in fusion — so the order is reproducible without a collation
engine. The lexical arm breaks cosine ties by NODE ID ascending; the fixture's ids are
assigned in `subjects` order (`Uuid::from_u128(position + 1)`), so an earlier subject wins a tie.
The rules under test, stated once: (1) lexical candidates = every OTHER note row with cosine
> 0, ordered (cosine desc, id asc), the EXCLUSION set dropped BEFORE truncation to 20 and
trashed candidates dropped AFTER it (the server's `names_for_ids` order); (2) the two HELD arms
are the server's own top-20 lists and only ever SHRINK under the client's fresher exclusion and
liveness; (3) RRF k=60, weights 1/1/1, the lexical arm weighted 0.4 when the subject's word
count is under 150; (4) an attachment subject has no vector and no lexical arm.
Tied cosines are constructed to be bit-identical (identical candidate vectors), never merely
close: two f32 results agree only when they are the same arithmetic.
Tags are interned into `dict` like lexemes — it is a string table. `excluded` lists the ids the
client's fresher exclusion set names BEYOND self. Synthetic fixture only — this crate is MIT
and ships in the public CLI mirror, so real workspace paths must never land here.
